thread:
Aisha Khan: heads up — hit intermittent cert verify errors during Dedicated onboarding when running our py-sdk tests through customer proxy/vpc. only under async load. passing verify='/etc/ssl/customer_ca.pem' to AsyncClient but still seeing failures. anyone seen this? :thinking:

Ben Patel: can you share a tiny repro? sync vs async matters here.

Aisha Khan: async. snippet: ```py
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(api_key='redacted', base_url='https://private.prod.internal', proxies={'https':'http://proxy.corp:3128'}, verify='/etc/ssl/customer_ca.pem')

# fired up 200 concurrent tasks each creating its own AsyncClient -> some TLS errors
```

Sally Kim: creating a client per task is a smell. connection pooling + sslcontext creation races have bitten us before. did you try sharing one AsyncClient?

Aisha Khan: yes — switching to a single shared AsyncClient dropped failures to almost zero. passing an explicit ssl.SSLContext also fixed it.

Ben Patel: sounds like we need to make SDK behavior deterministic: ensure we build SSLContext once at client init and reuse it for all pools and proxy code paths. also expose a first-class `ca_bundle` or `tls_config` parameter with typing so IDEs show it.

Aisha Khan: +1. my IDE didn't show a verify param on our wrapper so I missed it. typed arg would help users discover how to pass a PEM or SSLContext.

devex-bot: created ticket DEVEX-1512 to track reproducibility and DEVEX-1513 for SDK API addition (ca_bundle/tls_config).

Ben Patel: short-term advice for docs and support: 1) recommend sharing a single AsyncClient, 2) show example using ssl.SSLContext loaded with the full chain, and 3) recommend setting REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE env var as fallback. I'll add a quickstart snippet.

Sally Kim: also add test that spins up a small proxy simulator to return different intermediates so we don't regress.

Aisha Khan: will paste my test harness once I tidy it. thanks all. workaround summary: use a shared client or pass a pre-built ssl.SSLContext (and include full intermediate chain in the PEM).
